 Paris R1 previews and predictions: Tien vs. Tsitsipas, Nakashima vs. Berrettini 
 November 2, 2026 
 Ricky 
 Match previews 
 6 
 It is a tough draw in Paris for Learner Tien and Stefanos Tsitsipas, who have to face each other on Tuesday in a section that also includes Alexander Zverev and Novak Djokovic. Meanwhile, Brandon Nakashima kicks off his week against Matteo Berrettini. 
 Stefanos Tsitsipas vs. (15) Learner Tien
Tsitsipas has picked up some much-needed momentum dating back to the end of the post-Wimbledon clay swing. The 28-year-old Greek’s first half of the season was rough, but he is in contention for 2027 Australian Open seeding thanks to a title in Gstaad, a fourth-round showing at the U.S. Open, a fourth-round result in Shanghai, and a semifinal performance in Almaty.
Up first for Tsitsipas at the Rolex Paris Masters is a second showdown against Tien on Tuesday. Their only previous encounter came this spring on the red clay of Geneva, where the American left-hander prevailed 7-6(4), 7-6(2). Tien is coming down the stretch of a solid season that has him inside the top 20 (currently 19th). He may not be in absolute peak form at the moment, but if he can beat Tsitsipas on the red stuff then he definitely has a good chance to do it on a fast, low-bouncing hard court.
 Pick: Tien in 3

 (14) Brandon Nakashima vs. Matteo Berrettini
Nakashima and Berrettini will be squaring off for the third time in their careers and for the second time on this fall swing. They split their two previous meetings; Berrettini prevailed 4-6, 6-2, 7-6(5), 6-3 at the 2022 Australian Open , but Nakashima just recently got the job done 7-6(4), 7-5 at the Shanghai Masters.
 Andrew Patron/Delray Beach Open 
A second straight Masters 1000 battle should also favor Nakashima. The 18th-ranked American is a sparkling 71-35 lifetime on indoor hard courts; Berrettini is a mediocre 46-35. Neither man has ever won a match at this tournament, but both should be served well by the faster, lower-bouncing courts this year — and the result should be a high-quality contest. Nakashima beat Berrettini in straight sets in Shanghai even though he served 12 percentage points lower (69 to 57) and got out-aced by seven (12 to five). That bodes well for the 25-year-old’s chances on Tuesday.
 Pick: Nakashima in 3
